name: Bani
overview: Bani was a male warrior known as the Gadite and was the thirty-second member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not explicitly stated beyond his designation as a Gadite. No additional notes are recorded about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Bani means "descendant" in Hebrew. He is also referred to as Mibhar, which means "choice," indicating a possible alternate name or title. Neither name was given directly by God but reflects personal or familial naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Bani was the son of Hagri. Beyond this explicit familial connection, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Bani's significance in Scripture lies in his inclusion among David's elite warriors, known as "the thirty," highlighting his valor and trusted role in David's military leadership. His identification as a Gadite places him within one of the tribes of Israel, contributing to the diverse makeup of David's loyal men. Although details about his exploits are not provided, his mention underscores the importance of faithful service to God's anointed king.
